best_architecture: Recommended pattern for Local-Claw is a MemGPT/Letta-inspired tiered (OS-virtual-memory) architecture layered on top of the existing MongoDB + Chroma + Redis stack, organized by memory FUNCTION (cognitive tiers) rather than by storage engine. Three function tiers map cleanly onto the three datastores. (1) Core / working memory (the LLM's RAM): a small, always-in-context block holding the agent persona, current task/goal, the active file/repo summary, and a self-editable scratchpad of recent salient facts. Keep this in Redis (fast key-value, per-session) and inject it verbatim into every prompt. Budget it as a hard token cap (e.g. ~2-4k tokens of a ~8-32k window) so the rest of the window is free for retrieved evidence and reasoning. (2) Recall memory (disk cache): the raw, searchable conversation/turn + tool-call history. Store full transcripts and tool I/O in MongoDB (sessions/docs collections) with timestamps and metadata; index the searchable text in Chroma so the agent can semantically search its own history via a tool. (3) Archival memory (cold storage / long-term knowledge): processed, de-contextualized knowledge - code patterns, API/library facts, project conventions, learned skills - embedded into Chroma for vector retrieval, with the canonical records persisted in MongoDB. The three COGNITIVE memory types per CoALA taxonomy: EPISODIC (specific past sessions) lives in recall+archival; SEMANTIC (project facts, conventions) is extracted into archival; PROCEDURAL (verified reusable code skills, Voyager pattern) is a dedicated curated Chroma collection. Self-editing memory tools (core_memory_append, archival_memory_insert, etc.) + automatic background extraction (mem0 ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP) + recency/relevance/importance retrieval scoring (Generative Agents) + explicit token budgets.

pitfalls: Embedding-model drift: silently swapping or upgrading the embedding model (e.g. MiniLM -> bge) invalidates every stored vector because the new query vectors live in a different space, so retrieval recall collapses. Pin the embedding model + dimension per Chroma collection, store the model name/version in each record's metadata, and require a full re-embed migration on any model change. Local-Claw must treat the embedder as a versioned schema, not a swappable detail.

Memory bloat with no lifecycle/pruning: embedding everything and never deleting turns retrieval into noise - a six-month-old fact and yesterday's fact occupy the same similarity space, so top-k returns stale junk. Need TTL/decay on recall memory, importance scoring (Generative Agents recency+importance+relevance), de-duplication, and periodic consolidation of episodic -> semantic. 'Embed everything, retrieve top-k, stuff the window' is the dominant anti-pattern.

Context stuffing / window overload: pouring all retrieved memory into the prompt blows the budget, raises cost/latency, and degrades reasoning (lost-in-the-middle). Enforce a hard token cap on core memory (~2-4k) and on retrieved evidence separately; never let memory grow the prompt unboundedly. Gemma 4 / Qwen windows are finite - memory must be a budgeted citizen of the prompt.

Eviction killing durable state: naive FIFO/LRU eviction of working memory (or summarizing it away) destroys goal state - the 'Sisyphus Trap' (detail loss -> goal drift -> catastrophic restart). Flush salient facts from core memory down to archival BEFORE eviction; never let the only copy of the current task/goal live in an evictable buffer.

Duplicate / contradictory memories from append-only writes: naive 'always ADD' (the documented mem0 v2.0.0 ADD-only bug, issue #4896) leaves 'name is LGY' and 'name is LGS' both stored, making agent behavior unstable across turns. Use mem0-style LLM-judged UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP, or graph edge-invalidation, so corrections supersede rather than accumulate.

Expensive consolidation/reflection on the hot path: doing extraction, conflict resolution, and re-embedding synchronously inside the agent's turn spends the latency budget on bookkeeping instead of the task. Push consolidation to a background worker (Redis queue) and keep the read path fast.

N+1 / per-turn round trips to the vector DB: re-querying Chroma for every tool call, or one query per candidate fact during consolidation, serializes I/O. Batch embeddings and queries, cache hot results in Redis, and retrieve once per turn with a budget.

Cold-start with empty memory: a fresh agent has nothing to retrieve and either hallucinates conventions or wastes turns rediscovering the repo. Seed semantic/procedural collections from a first-run repo scan (README, config, conventions) and degrade gracefully when retrieval returns nothing.

Vector similarity is not importance or recency: cosine similarity surfaces what is semantically near, not what matters now or what changed; it cannot answer 'has this fact been superseded?'. Combine vector search with metadata filters (time, type, importance) and, for evolving facts, a temporal graph - do not rely on flat top-k alone.

Memory poisoning / prompt injection via stored content: untrusted tool output or user text written into memory is later retrieved and treated as authoritative instruction. Tag provenance, separate 'observed data' from 'instructions', and never let archival text override the system/persona block.

Summarize-at-write-time destroying episodic signal: compressing each turn into a generalization before it is needed collapses distinct episodes and loses the who/when/where needed for later reasoning. Store raw episodic traces in recall (MongoDB) and abstract to semantic only during deliberate consolidation.
bdd_gherkin_scenarios:
Feature: Memory persistence across sessions
  As Local-Claw
  I want long-term facts to survive process restarts
  So that a new session continues where the last left off

  Scenario: Recall a fact learned in a previous session
    Given session "s1" stored the semantic fact "project uses pnpm, not npm" in archival memory
    And the agent process is restarted with no in-memory state
    When a new session "s2" starts for the same project
    And the agent searches archival memory for "package manager"
    Then the result includes "project uses pnpm, not npm"
    And the fact's source session id and timestamp are returned with it

Feature: Semantic retrieval accuracy and token budget
  As Local-Claw
  I want relevant memories retrieved within a fixed token budget
  So that the prompt stays small and on-topic

  Scenario: Top-k semantic search returns relevant, budget-bounded results
    Given archival memory contains 500 mixed code-pattern and convention facts
    And the retrieval token budget is 1500 tokens
    When the agent searches for "how do we handle async errors in TypeScript skills"
    Then between 1 and 8 facts are returned ranked by relevance
    And the combined token count of returned facts is <= 1500
    And no returned fact embedding was produced by a different embedding model than the query

Feature: Memory conflict resolution (ADD / UPDATE / DELETE / NOOP)
  As the consolidation worker
  I want to reconcile new facts against existing ones
  So that memory stays non-redundant and contradiction-free

  Scenario Outline: Decide the correct operation for an incoming fact
    Given an existing memory "<existing>"
    When the consolidator evaluates the candidate fact "<candidate>"
    Then it performs operation "<op>"

    Examples:
      | existing                  | candidate                       | op     |
      | (none)                    | user prefers 2-space indent     | ADD    |
      | user prefers 2-space indent | user now prefers 4-space indent | UPDATE |
      | temp debug flag enabled   | debug flag removed from config  | DELETE |
      | project uses pnpm         | project uses pnpm               | NOOP   |

Feature: Procedural skill retrieval (Voyager pattern)
  As Local-Claw
  I want to reuse a verified skill instead of rewriting it
  So that solved problems are not re-solved

  Scenario: Retrieve a stored skill that matches the current sub-task
    Given a verified procedural skill "parse_csv_to_json" is stored in the procedural collection
    When the agent faces the sub-task "convert this CSV file into JSON"
    And it queries procedural memory before writing new code
    Then "parse_csv_to_json" is returned as the top match
    And the agent invokes the stored skill rather than generating new code

Feature: Memory pressure consolidation trigger
  As the memory manager
  I want core memory to stay under its token cap
  So that working memory never overflows the prompt budget

  Scenario: Overflow flushes salient facts to archival and frees core memory
    Given the core memory token cap is 3000 tokens
    And core memory currently holds 2900 tokens
    When the agent appends a 400-token block of new salient facts
    Then a consolidation job is enqueued on the background queue
    And the least-salient facts are flushed to archival memory durably
    And after flush the core memory token count is <= 3000
    And no flushed fact is lost (it is retrievable from archival)
optimal_implementation:
Implement a single async MemoryManager facade over Redis (working/core), MongoDB (sessions + canonical records), and Chroma (recall/archival/procedural vector collections). Embeddings are local via sentence-transformers so nothing leaves the A6000. Consolidation runs off the hot path on a Redis queue. The LLM interacts only through a small set of MCP tools.

```python
import asyncio, time, json, hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Literal, Optional
import redis.asyncio as aioredis
from motor.motor_asyncio import AsyncIOMotorClient
import chromadb
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

EMBED_MODEL_NAME = "BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5"  # pinned; stored in metadata
CORE_TOKEN_CAP = 3000
RETRIEVE_TOKEN_BUDGET = 1500
MemType = Literal["episodic", "semantic", "procedural"]
Op = Literal["ADD", "UPDATE", "DELETE", "NOOP"]

@dataclass
class MemoryRecord:
    text: str
    mem_type: MemType
    session_id: str
    importance: float = 0.5
    created_at: float = field(default_factory=time.time)
    source: str = "agent"          # provenance, for poisoning defense
    embed_model: str = EMBED_MODEL_NAME
    id: str = ""
    def __post_init__(self):
        if not self.id:
            self.id = hashlib.sha1(f"{self.session_id}:{self.text}".encode()).hexdigest()

def count_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    return max(1, len(text) // 4)  # replace with the model tokenizer

class MemoryManager:
    def __init__(self, redis_url, mongo_url, chroma_path):
        self.r = aioredis.from_url(redis_url, decode_responses=True)
        self.mongo = AsyncIOMotorClient(mongo_url).localclaw
        self.chroma = chromadb.PersistentClient(path=chroma_path)
        self._embedder = SentenceTransformer(EMBED_MODEL_NAME)
        # one collection per type; pin embedding model in collection metadata
        self.cols = {t: self.chroma.get_or_create_collection(
            name=f"mem_{t}", metadata={"embed_model": EMBED_MODEL_NAME})
            for t in ("episodic", "semantic", "procedural")}

    async def _embed(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        return await asyncio.to_thread(
            lambda: self._embedder.encode(texts, normalize_embeddings=True).tolist())

    # ---- WORKING / CORE MEMORY (Redis) ----
    async def get_core(self, session_id: str) -> str:
        return await self.r.get(f"core:{session_id}") or ""

    async def core_append(self, session_id: str, block: str) -> None:
        key = f"core:{session_id}"
        cur = await self.r.get(key) or ""
        new = (cur + "\n" + block).strip()
        await self.r.set(key, new)
        if count_tokens(new) > CORE_TOKEN_CAP:
            await self._enqueue_consolidation(session_id)  # off hot path

    # ---- RECALL (MongoDB raw) + index in Chroma episodic ----
    async def log_turn(self, session_id: str, role: str, content: str,
                       tool_io: Optional[dict] = None) -> None:
        await self.mongo.sessions.insert_one(
            {"session_id": session_id, "role": role, "content": content,
             "tool_io": tool_io, "ts": time.time()})

    # ---- STORE durable memory (canonical Mongo + vector Chroma) ----
    async def store(self, rec: MemoryRecord) -> str:
        await self.mongo.memories.update_one(
            {"_id": rec.id}, {"$set": rec.__dict__}, upsert=True)
        vec = (await self._embed([rec.text]))[0]
        self.cols[rec.mem_type].upsert(
            ids=[rec.id], embeddings=[vec], documents=[rec.text],
            metadatas=[{"session_id": rec.session_id, "importance": rec.importance,
                        "created_at": rec.created_at, "embed_model": rec.embed_model,
                        "source": rec.source}])
        return rec.id

    # ---- SEARCH (budgeted, recency+importance+relevance reranked) ----
    async def search(self, query: str, mem_type: MemType, k: int = 8,
                     budget: int = RETRIEVE_TOKEN_BUDGET) -> list[dict]:
        qv = (await self._embed([query]))[0]
        res = self.cols[mem_type].query(query_embeddings=[qv], n_results=k,
                                        include=["documents", "metadatas", "distances"])
        now = time.time(); scored = []
        for doc, md, dist in zip(res["documents"][0], res["metadatas"][0], res["distances"][0]):
            relevance = 1 - dist
            recency = 0.99 ** ((now - md["created_at"]) / 3600)
            score = 0.6*relevance + 0.25*md["importance"] + 0.15*recency
            scored.append((score, doc, md))
        scored.sort(reverse=True, key=lambda x: x[0])
        out, used = [], 0
        for score, doc, md in scored:
            t = count_tokens(doc)
            if used + t > budget: break
            used += t; out.append({"text": doc, "score": score, "meta": md})
        return out

    # ---- CONFLICT RESOLUTION (mem0-style, LLM-judged) ----
    async def reconcile(self, candidate: MemoryRecord, llm_decide) -> Op:
        similar = await self.search(candidate.text, candidate.mem_type, k=5, budget=2000)
        op: Op = await llm_decide(candidate.text, similar)  # returns ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP
        if op == "ADD":     await self.store(candidate)
        elif op == "UPDATE": await self.store(candidate)        # upsert by id supersedes
        elif op == "DELETE":
            for s in similar:
                self.cols[candidate.mem_type].delete(ids=[s["meta"].get("id", "")])
        return op

    # ---- BACKGROUND CONSOLIDATION (off hot path) ----
    async def _enqueue_consolidation(self, session_id: str) -> None:
        await self.r.lpush("consolidate:q", session_id)

    async def consolidation_worker(self, llm_extract, llm_decide):
        while True:
            _, session_id = await self.r.brpop("consolidate:q")
            core = await self.get_core(session_id)
            facts = await llm_extract(core)            # extract salient facts
            for f in facts:
                rec = MemoryRecord(text=f, mem_type="semantic", session_id=session_id)
                await self.reconcile(rec, llm_decide)  # ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP
            # trim core to least-salient until under cap (flush already durable)
            await self._trim_core(session_id)

    async def _trim_core(self, session_id: str) -> None:
        key = f"core:{session_id}"; text = await self.r.get(key) or ""
        lines = [l for l in text.splitlines() if l.strip()]
        while count_tokens("\n".join(lines)) > CORE_TOKEN_CAP and lines:
            lines.pop(0)  # oldest first; salient facts already flushed to archival
        await self.r.set(key, "\n".join(lines))
```

MCP TOOL INTERFACE exposed to the LLM (thin wrappers on the manager; the model never touches the stores directly):
```python
# core_memory_append(block: str) -> ok           # edit working memory
# core_memory_replace(old: str, new: str) -> ok
# archival_memory_insert(text, mem_type) -> id    # write durable knowledge
# archival_memory_search(query, mem_type, k) -> [facts]  # semantic recall
# recall_search(query, k) -> [past turns]         # search raw conversation history
# procedural_search(task) -> [skill]              # Voyager skill reuse before coding
```

KEY DESIGN RULES baked in: (1) embedding model name pinned in every record + collection metadata; reject queries whose model differs (drift guard). (2) Hard token caps on both core memory and retrieval. (3) All extraction/conflict-resolution runs in consolidation_worker via the Redis queue, never inline. (4) Conflict resolution is LLM-judged ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP, upsert-by-id so UPDATE supersedes rather than duplicates. (5) Provenance (source) stored on every record for poisoning defense. (6) Retrieval reranks by relevance+importance+recency (Generative Agents), not raw cosine. (7) Raw episodic turns kept in MongoDB; abstraction to semantic happens only during deliberate consolidation.
sota_improvements: Temporal/bi-temporal knowledge graph (Zep/Graphiti, arxiv:2501.13956): upgrade evolving facts from flat vectors to a graph where every edge carries valid-time AND transaction-time, enabling point-in-time queries ('what did this config look like in March?') and edge INVALIDATION instead of deletion - so corrections never produce contradictory duplicates. Zep beats MemGPT on DMR (94.8% vs 93.4%) and gains up to 18.5% on LongMemEval with ~90% lower latency. Add graphiti-core as an optional fourth store for entity/relationship facts while keeping Chroma for unstructured semantic recall.

Graph-augmented entity-relationship memory (mem0g / HippocRAG): model who/what/owns/depends-on as a graph so multi-hop questions vector similarity cannot answer ('who owns this module and has ownership changed?') become traversals; HippocRAG-style PageRank over a KG improves multi-hop retrieval.

LLM-judged conflict resolution over naive append (mem0 ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP, arxiv:2504.19413): replace the documented append-only failure (mem0 issue #4896, duplicate contradictory facts) with the retrieve-similar-then-LLM-decide pipeline already wired into the implementation - the single biggest correctness win over a plain vector store.

Episodic vs semantic retrieval ROUTING (arxiv:2502.06975, GSW/SYNAPSE): route the query rather than blindly top-k - factual 'what is our convention' hits the semantic store, 'how did we solve X before' retrieves prior trajectories from episodic, 'reuse a skill' hits procedural. GSW reports F1 0.850 (+20% over RAG) with 51% fewer query-time tokens by using structured situation representations instead of raw retrieval.

Self-RAG / memory-quality gating: have the model critique and grade retrieved memories before using them (reflect-on-retrieval) and grade candidate facts before writing, filtering low-importance or low-confidence items - directly counters memory bloat and poisoning.

Continual-learning / reflection patterns (Voyager skill library + Reflexion/A-MEM): periodically distill successful episodic trajectories into reusable, verified procedural skills and reflective summaries, growing a curated skill library over time rather than re-solving problems - turns the procedural Chroma collection into a compounding asset.

Importance-weighted decay + active forgetting (Generative Agents): add explicit recency+importance+relevance scoring (already in the impl) plus scheduled pruning/forgetting so memory is curated, not just accumulated - the field's consensus move from 'RAG-as-memory' to 'agentic memory' with full lifecycle management.
uncertain: [uncertain] Exact optimal core-memory token cap (2-4k) and the relevance/importance/recency weights (0.6/0.25/0.15) are starting heuristics that should be tuned empirically against Local-Claw's Gemma 4 / Qwen2.5-Coder context windows and task mix.

[uncertain] Whether to adopt graphiti-core (temporal KG) at v1 or defer it: it adds a Neo4j/graph dependency beyond the current MongoDB+Chroma+Redis stack; recommended as a phase-2 upgrade once flat-vector memory is proven.
